Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testNegativeNumber` tries to parse a command line with a negative numerical argument for the option "num". However, the parser mistakes the negative number `-42` for another option and throws an error. This behavior indicates that the parser is not handling negative numerical arguments correctly.

Looking at the test case, the parser is configured with an option "num" that expects a numerical argument. When parsing `--num -42`, the parser incorrectly interprets `-42` as a separate option instead of the argument for the "num" option.

To identify the root cause, we need to examine how the parser handles numerical arguments and the parsing logic for options in the Apache Commons CLI library.

Next, I will inspect relevant methods in the Apache Commons CLI library to understand how numerical arguments are processed and options are parsed.

After analyzing the relevant methods in the Apache Commons CLI library, the issue in the failing test `testNegativeNumber` seems to be due to how the parser handles negative numerical arguments. Here is a step-by-step explanation of the bug:

1. The test case creates an argument `numArg` using `ArgumentBuilder.withValidator(NumberValidator.getNumberInstance())`, which expects a numerical value.
2. An option `numOpt` is created with this argument using `DefaultOptionBuilder.withLongName("num").withArgument(numArg)`.
3. The option `numOpt` is added to a group `options` using `GroupBuilder.withOption(numOpt)`.
4. When the test case tries to parse the command line with `--num -42` using `Parser.parse(new String[] {...})`, the parser mistakenly interprets `-42` as a separate option instead of the argument for the "num" option.
5. This leads to the parser throwing an error as it doesn't expect a standalone option `-42`.

To fix this issue, the parser logic needs to be modified to correctly handle negative numerical arguments for options in the Apache Commons CLI library.

The best locations to fix this issue would be:
```
org.apache.commons.cli2.commandline.Parser.parse(String[])
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
